correctness.rationale: In the normalized convex class K, f(z)=sqrt((1+z)/(1-z))−1 maps the disk onto a translated convex sector and has f(0)=0,f′(0)=1. In Cayley coordinate w=(1+z)/(1−z), A=zg′/g=(1+w)(1+sqrt(w))/(4sqrt(w)), P=1+zg′′/g′=(1+3w²)/(4w). Direct simplification of the exact Grigoriciuc functional gives hα=(1−α)/Dα+Cα/P, Dα=1−α+αA, Cα=α[(1−α)(A²+1)+(2α−1)A]/Dα. At w0=i/sqrt(3), writing A=u+iv yields u>1/2, v>0 and Im Cα=α(1−α)v[α((u−1)²+v²)+2u−1]/[(1−α+αu)²+α²v²]>0 for EVERY 0<α<1. For w=iy, y approaches 1/sqrt(3) from below: P=i(3y²−1)/(4y) tends to zero in the negative imaginary direction, so Re(C/P) tends to −infinity; move w into Re w>0 by continuity for genuine interior points. For endpoints h0≡1 and h1=1/P, Re P>0 by convexity. The residue sign is uniform in the quantifier α∈(0,1) analytically; source verify_pole.py was read and separate sympy/numeric evaluations corroborated identities, not used as a proof of the universal assertion.
